bindingNotes: Semantic summaries only, not canonical wire fixtures. operation.timestampMinutesAgo is a synthetic ordering fact to bind to wire timestamps; requiredSourceVersions is a consumer coverage fact, not an added wire field.
Within each milestone, key latest attempts by sourceVersion only, not runId; newest timestamp wins and ties take the worse verdict.
evidence-absent means no snapshot. S1b absent means an accepted snapshot with zero operations and every enabled milestone unproven.
requiredItemProof unknown means a pending or missing latest attempt for a listed version (S1b partial and partial-within-milestone). State counts are display facts, not verdict inputs.
freshness fresh/stale/unknown maps to S1b freshness. For unknown ignore S1b stale. The freshness overlay takes precedence over state.availability. Acceptance time is supplied by the consumer.
Preserved means verified custody only: verifiedNotIndexed + indexed; receivedOnly is excluded. Merged S1c corrected the S1b producer.
Schema-required proof fields are checked before semantic stage grading. Complete proof can still be cross-version or non-proving; that is unproven, not schema rejection.
Attribution of the schema rulings: docs/sessions/S1c.md, rulings 1–8 and section D; decision 2026-10-04 23:50.

Fields omitted from operation summaries and surrounding envelopes are otherwise schema-valid by premise. Schema-failure cases deliberately omit the specified proof or violate the stated count consistency only. These summaries are never submitted as wire envelopes.

Round-4 clarification incorporated in merged S1c: observedAt caps the selected timestamp whether it is a known lastSuccessfulSync or the consumer acceptance fallback. Historically, the original S1c ruling 5 bounded only the fallback in its wording.

Hash comparisons apply only to latest attempts after whole-snapshot schema validation. Null mismatches an approved non-null hash for every milestone, including ingest-custody. A blocking stage or failed result still outranks a hash mismatch.

Blocking stages affect the operation milestone only, not unrelated enabled milestones. A bad-order truncated snapshot is the separate whole-snapshot rule: every enabled milestone becomes unproven, including any with a visible failed attempt.

Producer-only omittedLatestAttempts is a synthetic full-inventory fact, never a wire field. producerSemanticSuccessClaim must not be read as a consumer expectation; consumerVerdict is evaluated using only the visible snapshot.

Grade every co-latest attempt at the newest timestamp before selecting the worst tie outcome: include hash binding, exact source-version proof, stage and result. Do not select a stage-only winner and bind its hashes afterward. Older semantic mismatches stay superseded; input order must not change the verdict.

Truncation ordering checks latest attempts for every operation milestone, including disabled milestones. A visible verified attempt before a disabled pending attempt makes a truncated snapshot unproven for all enabled milestones; without truncation the disabled milestone has no effect on them.

semanticExpectationCheck.assertionDefinition: Select cases whose category equals evidence-semantics. For each expected member whose key is in checkedExpectedFields, count one top-level equality assertion. An object-valued member counts once. Other expected fields are descriptive and are not included in this local oracle count.
semanticExpectationCheck.scope: Historical round-4 standalone semantic contract oracle only; these are local review results, not production-runtime tests. Source runtimes, canonical wire-schema validation, signatures and filesystem integration were not executed in these checks. The later schema-and-fixture reference binding does not expand these execution claims or counts.
